status_note: Nine clips queued, eight delivered and staged, all eight rejected at Pass A on 4 Aug 2026. The batch cannot answer the probe's question: every clip is conditioned on a reference still whose view id is wrong, so each prompt asked for an opening frame and a camera start that cannot both be satisfied. See day_1_result. No clip is marked terminally failed; the remedy is upstream.
observed_truth_rule: Only independently AI-reviewed Pass B claims, with required owner adjudication resolved, may be scored as gold. Unchanged from the parent dataset.
wall: Synthetic video is development evidence. No result from this dataset promotes a capture-strategy claim, a compare claim, or a product accuracy claim. docs/26 still resolves photo-vs-video on real capture.

generation_policy.path: Gemini Omni subscription surface, operated by the project owner
generation_policy.note: Inherits the parent dataset's permanent restriction: no metered generation endpoint. The budget is a hard per-day ceiling that includes retries.

gemini-omni-video.note: Same provider as the parent dataset's Google image arm. Any comparison against that arm is a service comparison within one provider, not an independent-provider comparison.

reference_frame_policy.rule: Every clip is conditioned on one still from the parent dataset, pinned by path and SHA-256.
reference_frame_policy.reason: Room identity is the thing that drifts. The parent pilot's 36% first-attempt rejection rate was overwhelmingly continuity failure across four static views; a moving camera has strictly more drift surface, so identity is pinned to an artefact rather than to prose.
reference_frame_policy.eligible_source: images/google/gemini-omni/*, restricted to the nine scenarios holding a complete four-view Omni packet

provenance_gate.fact: The 57 Gemini Omni stills are not in the parent tasks.csv at all. They have owner review and no recorded Pass A.
provenance_gate.required: docs/31 Amendment B work order item 6 — the Gemini Omni Pass A import — which that work order names in advance as the droppable item if the schedule slips.
provenance_gate.effect: Until the import lands, every clip here is conditioned on an artefact with no recorded provenance. build_video_tasks.py refuses to write the queue unless --allow-unimported-reference is passed, and stamps reference_provenance on every row.
provenance_gate.inherited_risk: If item 6 is dropped, this probe's reference frames never acquire recorded provenance and the probe cannot produce gold. It is gated on the one item most likely to be cut.

realised_harm.fact: The risk landed. The stills are not merely unreviewed, they are mislabelled: stage_gemini_omni_prior_batches.py assigns A-wide, B-reverse, C-inventory, D-condition positionally in the operator's supplied order, and that order was reversed. The file named <scenario>-A-wide.jpeg is the packet's condition detail.
realised_harm.evidence: evals/synthetic/audit_gemini_omni_views.py. Four source filenames state their own view id; all four contradict the id they were filed under and all four fit an exactly reversed order, with none contradicting it. Across all nine packets, the file filed as A-wide names a condition view: five say 'condition' outright, two of those say 'D-condition'.
realised_harm.scope: The 36 stills staged through the positional route are suspect. The 21 staged through import_gemini_omni_batch.py name a view per file and show no contradiction. Every Phase 3.6 reference frame comes from the affected route.
realised_harm.consequence: Pass A is where 'is this the view it claims to be' is caught. Work order item 6 is not the droppable item; it is the prerequisite for this probe.

terms_and_publication.basis: docs/31 Amendment B B9. UK Google consumer terms prohibit using output to develop machine-learning models or related AI technology, and the whole Google arm is excluded on terms grounds. Video output from Gemini Omni inherits this without exception.

acceptance_criteria: The opening frame matches the pinned reference frame in layout, fittings, finishes and lighting.
Every element of the clip's continuity list holds for the whole take; nothing morphs, gains, or loses identity mid-move.
Every required evidence item is legible in at least one frame.
No enumerated negative control is rendered as a real defect.
No unenumerated material difference from the reference frame appears at any point in the take.
One unbroken take: no cuts, dissolves, speed ramps, titles, borders or annotations.
No people, no readable text, no logos, no watermark.
Geometry stays coherent through camera motion: no furniture sliding, no doorways changing count or position, no room growing.
Audio matches the clip's declared audio mode exactly, including the silent case.

review_policy.video_addendum: Pass A samples frames at a fixed cadence (1 fps) plus every declared gold timestamp. Continuity is judged across the sampled strip, not on a single frame. Any accepted clip records the sampled strip's hash alongside the clip hash.
review_policy.reviewers: Primary claude-sonnet-4-6, second gemini-3.5-flash-low, both through the Antigravity CLI on local frames, no metered endpoint. The primary is deliberately not the generator's model family. The second is the parent dataset's Pass A reviewer and IS the generator's family; it is kept for comparability with the image arm and is not counted as independent-family confirmation.
review_policy.measured_not_reviewed: one_unbroken_take, audio mode and container facts are decided by ffmpeg in build_video_strip.py and handed to the reviewers as findings they are told not to re-litigate. A measured failure escalates to the owner rather than being reconciled by two reviewers who could not observe it.

day_1_result.verdict: Void for its stated question, not a negative result about the generator. The dominant hard failure is 'opening frame does not match reference', which the mislabelled reference frames caused by construction: a prompt that pins a floor-level close-up as the opening frame and also says 'start at the doorway and pivot across the room' cannot be satisfied. Do not record this as evidence that Gemini Omni cannot hold a room through motion.
findings_independent_of_the_reference_de: Readable brands or product text appear in 6 of 8 clips (Apple, Samsung, Beko, Fairy, and legible cleaning-product labels) despite an explicit avoid list covering logos and readable text. This is acceptance criterion 7 and does not depend on which frame was the reference.

Geometry breaks mid-take with no scene cut: VU-1.RP-003's floor covering changes from wood-plank LVT to stone-look tile between sampled frames 4 and 7 and its cabinetry morphs between frames 3 and 4; VU-1.RP-024's desk moves from the left wall to the window wall between frames 7 and 8; VU-2's closed door becomes an open doorway between frames 4 and 5.

VU-5.RP-019-hold breaches its own must-never-be-visible list: the primary reviewer places the rear floor and lower rear wall in frames 7, 9 and 10. The second reviewer recorded no breach. Independent visual inspection agrees with the primary: the camera advances well past the doorway it was told to hold. The counterfactual pair therefore has no valid control arm.

6 of 7 clips declared silent carry an audible track, peaking between -41 and -22 dBFS in discrete bursts rather than stationary room tone. The generation prompt asked for no speech, no music, no sound effects and no room tone.
VU-4.RP-022-slow ends on an almost entirely black frame at t=9.958.
day_1_result.partial_positive: VU-2 room naming worked: both reviewers named Entrance hall then Kitchen. Their boundary brackets disagree by two seconds (sampled frame 7 versus 9), which is the resolution limit of a 1 fps strip, not a segmentation result.
day_1_result.budget: Nine of ten day-1 clips were spent. Two of them (VU-1.RP-024 and the VU-4 rungs) are day-2-or-later work under docs/34 and should not have been generated on day 1.
